overall.sentence: Gate-controlled loading of localized anyons with an anti-dot inside an interferometer was shown before in a GaAs Mach-Zehnder device (arXiv:2410.16488, cited as [54]); what is new here is the bilayer-graphene Fabry-Perot platform and its extension to even-denominator states, which a concurrent paper from another group (arXiv:2603.11162, posted the same day and not cited) also reports.

assessment.claim: Headline (claim 1): gate-controlled anti-dot in a BLG Fabry-Perot interferometer gives hundreds of reproducible discrete phase slips in five FQH states
assessment.note: Ghosh et al. loaded localized anyons with a gate-defined anti-dot in a GaAs Mach-Zehnder interferometer (same question and method, different system); the BLG FPI platform and five states incl. even-denominator are new. Concurrent 2603.11162 matches all three facets but was posted the same day.

assessment.claim: Claim 2: interfering edge charge equals the fractional part of the filling (e/2 at 1+1/2, 2e/5 at -2/5)
assessment.note: Kim et al. reported the same Aharonov-Bohm charge in BLG FPIs incl. e/2 at even-denominator states; the paper credits this ('agreeing with recent work [13]') and makes no priority claim, so no item.

assessment.claim: Claim 3: abelian slip sizes 2pi/3 and 2pi/5 match e/3 and e/5 braiding phases
assessment.note: Discrete 2pi/3 slips from single quasiparticles entering the bulk were seen in a graphene FPI (Samuelson et al., [11]) and e/5 localized charge with 2e/5 edge in GaAs (Nakamura et al., [48]); new is gate-controlled loading in BLG. The paper cites these.

assessment.claim: Claim 4 and abstract: controlled population of localized e/4 anyons at 1+1/2, 'significant milestone', 'direct measurement of charge 1/4'
assessment.note: Localized e/4 in BLG FPIs was inferred earlier from phase-fluctuation statistics ([13]) and e/4 charge by SET and shot noise ([59],[60]); the controlled anti-dot loading is the new facet, and concurrent 2603.11162 reports the same in BLG.

assessment.claim: Claim 5: localized charge from slip spacing and anti-dot radius excludes charge e
assessment.note: Anti-dot charge spectroscopy of fractional quasiparticles in BLG ([53]) and graphene anti-dots (Mills, Averin, Du, PRL 2020, [52]) precede it; new is doing it inside an interferometer. Search was weak (arXiv API failed), so no stronger grade is given.

positioning: The paper sits at the meeting point of three lines it largely cites: anyon braiding from stochastic bulk quasiparticles in graphene FPIs ([10]-[13], [34]), anti-dot charge spectroscopy in graphene ([52], [53]), and gate-controlled anti-dot loading in a GaAs Mach-Zehnder interferometer ([54], [55]). What it adds, as far as these web searches show, is controlled anti-dot loading inside a bilayer-graphene Fabry-Perot interferometer across five states including the even-denominator 1+1/2, plus the per-Landau-level recurrence of slip regions. A concurrent Weizmann paper (arXiv:2603.11162, posted the same day) uses the same platform and anti-dot idea for e/2-e/4 braiding and is not cited; the arXiv API failed throughout (HTTP 429), so coverage rests on web search and the reference list.

issues.claim: Controlled population of localized e/4 anyons in a BLG interferometer
issues.headline: Cite the concurrent BLG anti-dot braiding paper (arXiv:2603.11162)
issues.issue: Kim et al., 'Selective braiding of different anyons in the even-denominator fractional quantum Hall effect' (arXiv:2603.11162), posted the same day, uses a gate-defined anti-dot in a BLG Fabry-Perot interferometer to control localized e/4 anyons. The paper calls this a milestone without mentioning that work; referees will know it.

evidence.quote: Controlling the population of localized e/4 anyons in an interferometer marks a significant milestone towards observing their non-local exchange statistics

issues.fix: Cite arXiv:2603.11162 as concurrent independent work where the contribution is stated (introduction and conclusion), and say what differs: five states, slip counting and spacing, the per-Landau-level recurrence.

issues.claim: Direct measurement of localized charge e/4
issues.headline: 'Direct measurement' of e/4 is stronger than the inference supports
issues.issue: The e/4 value is inferred from slip spacing with an assumed anti-dot radius of 150-200 nm and from a slip size of 0.221(30) of 2pi, and e/4 at even-denominator states was measured before (SET [59], shot noise [60], BLG interferometry statistics in arXiv:2412.19886 [13]). 'Direct' invites a referee to object.

evidence.quote: In all cases, the charge of the quasiparticles extracted through the phase slip events is close to the fundamental anyon quasiparticle charge, culminating in the direct measurement of charge

issues.fix: Replace 'direct measurement' with 'an interferometric estimate consistent with', and name the earlier e/4 measurements in the same sentence.

edit.before: culminating in the direct measurement of charge
edit.after: culminating in an interferometric estimate, consistent with earlier measurements [13, 59, 60], of charge
